findings.text: test_shipped_routing_default_is_route writes routing:\n  picker: route into its own tmp_path fixture and asserts that fixture resolves as route with provenance shipped, so it no longer reads the repository's shipped default. reckon/schema/flight-defaults.yaml still reads picker: shadow (owned by the concurrent picker-routes-by-default node), so between this node and that flip no test in this file pins the real shipped value. This is precisely what the node's done-when asked for, so it does not hold the node; the coverage is restored when the flip node lands and should be confirmed then.

The after_suite field names revision b99856e93377b9c95409bc9d834e867d288158a7, but logs/head_gate.log's own first line reads 'revision: working tree (base 6058ff38617a187e0a480a0de1486c2b81b885ef + uncommitted node changes)' and its mtime (04:45:00) precedes the commit (04:47:22). The head gate therefore ran on the working tree, and the record asserts a revision its log does not. The substance is intact — the worktree is clean at b99856e9 and the reviewer reproduced the node's new case green at that head — but a reader comparing the two arms cannot tie the head arm to the commit from the log alone.

No in-repo caller currently reaches the new branch: all five plan_dispatch call sites either pin route="deterministic" (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5198 and 10803) or pass a selection (reckon/cli.py:1758 and reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5736, 5893), and dispatch_picker_selection always returns a dict. The done-when's 'including dry runs and internal re-dispatch paths' is therefore demonstrated only by the node's direct test rather than by a production caller, which is worth confirming once the routing default flips to route and a caller that omits the selection exists.
